controlled_same_host_comparison.interpretation: For this fixed 4097-point, 16-shard V1 profile on this host, four selected devices preserved exact output but were slower than two selected devices.
controlled_same_host_comparison.timing_scope: adapter end-to-end diagnostic timing emitted by each accepted repeat; no warm-up benchmark protocol and no speedup acceptance gate

implementation_boundary.eight_device_inference: The controlled 2-to-4 result suggests that selecting eight devices for this fixed profile is unlikely to improve end-to-end time, but no eight-device timing claim is made.
implementation_boundary.nvlink_caveat: NVLink would not automatically accelerate V1 because V1 emits zero inter-device peer bytes. A peer-aware redesign would be a new implementation policy and would require fresh evidence.

interpretation: All five accepted artifacts were produced by the protected manual hardware workflow from the same accepted main commit.
All fifteen physical CUDA executions produced the same complete-path SHA-256 and the same maximum reference residuals.
The campaign establishes cross-host, cross-device-count and Ampere-to-Ada reproducibility for this bounded profile.
The controlled same-host comparison does not support a local speedup claim when increasing selected RTX 4070 Ti SUPER devices from two to four.
These observations do not establish distributed execution, universal speedup, geometry receipt authority, or an eight-device result.
The diagnostic timing comparison is not a published speedup benchmark because the V1 trusted workflow does not include a separate warm-up/measurement protocol.
